s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic photosensitive eruption with systemic and cutaneous manifestations
salient_findings: Photosensitive eruption involving face, neck, trunk, and extremities
Violaceous erythema on forehead and midface
Diffuse poikiloderma involving upper chest, anterolateral thighs, and extensor arms
key_facts: Previous treatments tried: systemic steroids, hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, tofacitinib, rituximab, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG)
Elevated serum IFN-β levels (8 pg/mL, normal ≤2 pg/mL)

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic photosensitive eruption with systemic and cutaneous manifestations
salient_findings: Photosensitive eruption involving face, neck, trunk, and extremities
Violaceous erythema on forehead and midface
Diffuse poikiloderma involving upper chest, anterolateral thighs, and extensor arms
key_facts: Previous treatments tried: systemic steroids, hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, tofacitinib, rituximab, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG)
Elevated serum IFN-β levels (8 pg/mL, normal ≤2 pg/mL)

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical examination revealed violaceous erythema, diffuse poikiloderma, and erythematous papules, consistent with dermatomyositis, and laboratory tests showed elevated serum IFN-β levels and presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies, which are characteristic of this disease

shortlist.label: Lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms, including photosensitive eruption and systemic manifestations, are consistent with lupus erythematosus, and the presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies is also seen in this disease

shortlist.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's clinical presentation, including dermatomyositis-like skin changes, myositis, and presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies, overlaps with features of mixed connective tissue disease

shortlist.label: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's age of onset and duration of symptoms, as well as the presence of systemic and cutaneous manifestations, are consistent with juvenile idiopathic arthritis

shortlist.label: Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's clinical presentation, including poikiloderma and nailfold changes, is consistent with scleroderma, although the absence of other characteristic features, such as sclerodactyly, makes this diagnosis less likely
